excerpt: An Bille fá Straitéis um Choimirciú Aosach, 2026 Adult Safeguarding Strategy Bill 2026 Mar a tionscnaíodh As initiated [No. 79 of 2026] AN BILLE FÁ STRAITÉIS UM CHOIMIRCIÚ AOSACH, 2026 ADULT SAFEGUARDING STRATEGY BILL 2026 Mar a tionscnaíodh As initiated CONTENTS Section 1. Short title SCHEDULE RELEVANT SERVICE [No. 79 of 2026] ACTS REFERRED TO Companies Act 2014 (No. 38) Health Act 2007 (No. 23) Mental Health Act 2001 (No. 25) National Vetting Bureau (Children and Vulnerable Persons) Act 2012 (No. 47) 2 AN BILLE FÁ STRAITÉIS UM CHOIMIRCIÚ AOSACH, 2026 ADULT SAFEGUARDING STRATEGY BILL 2026 Bill entitled An Act to require the Minister for Health to prepare periodic strategic plans for the purpose of protecting certain persons who are at risk of harm, to make certain provisions in relation to the implementation and review of such strategic plans and to provide for related matters. Be it enacted by the Oireachtas as follows: Interpretation 1. In this Act— “adult” means a person who has reached the age of 18 years; “adult at risk” means an adult who, at any particular time, by reason of the person’s physical or mental condition or other particular characteristics or family or life circumstance (whether permanent or otherwise) needs support to protect against harm to that person; “adult safeguarding” means measures that are, or may be, put in place to promote the health, safety and welfare of adults at risk, including measures to— (a) minimise the risk of harm to such adults, and (b) support such adults to protect themselves from harm; “adult safeguarding strategy” shall be read in accordance with section 2; “Minister” means the Minister for Health; “public authority” means— (a) a Minister of the Government, (b) a board, authority or other body, other than a company under the Companies Act 2014, established by or under statute, (c) a company under the Companies Act 2014 in which all the shares are held— (i) by or on behalf of a Minister of the Government, or (ii) by directors appointed by a Minister of the Government, or 3 5 10 15 20 25 30 (d) a company under the Companies Act 2014 in which all the shares are held by a board, authority or body referred to in paragraph (b) or by a company referred to in paragraph (c). Adult safeguarding strategy 2. (1) The Minister shall— (a) not later than 6 months after this Act comes into operation, prepare and adopt an adult safeguarding strategy in respect of the period of 3 years commencing on the date on which the strategy is adopted, and (b) within the period of 3 months before each third anniversary of the date on which an adult safeguarding strategy is adopted under paragraph (a), prepare and adopt an adult safeguarding strategy in respect of the period of 3 years commencing on the date of that anniversary. (2) An adult safeguarding strategy shall— (a) specify such objectives for the period concerned as the Minister considers appropriate in respect of adult safeguarding, (b) specify such measures to be taken during the period concerned as the Minister considers appropriate in respect of adult safeguarding, (c) where relevant, specify any legislative or other regulatory measures that is proposed to be duly adopted for the purpose of achieving any objective specified in paragraph (a) or taking any measure under paragraph (b), and (d) specify such other matters as the Minister considers appropriate. (3) An objective or measure specified for the purpose of subsection (2) may apply— (a) in respect of public authorities generally, (b) in respect of a particular public authority, or (c) in respect of a particular class of public authorities. (4) An adult safeguarding strategy shall, in particular, include objectives and measures in respect of each of the following: (a) the duties that shall apply in respect of persons providing relevant services for the purpose of adult safeguarding, including— (i) the identification of any potential for abuse or other harm that may occur to an adult at risk in relation to the provision of such services, including by means of risk assessments, and (ii) the adoption of appropriate policies and procedures and the taking of appropriate measures to ensure, in so far as is practicable, that an adult at risk, while availing of such services, is protected from any abuse or other harm; (b) ensuring appropriate oversight and regulat

title: Protection of Voice and Image Bill 2025
excerpt: ___________ An Bille um Chosaint Glóir agus Íomhá, 2025 Protection of Voice and Image Bill 2025 ___________ Meabhrán Míniúcháin Explanatory Memorandum ___________ 1 ____________ AN BILLE UM CHOSAINT GLÓIR AGUS ÍOMHÁ, 2025 PROTECTION OF VOICE AND IMAGE BILL 2025 ____________ EXPLANATORY MEMORANDUM ____________ Introduction The purpose of this Bill is to create specific offences for the misuse of an individual’s name, photograph, voice or likeness. This is to address the growing problem of deepfakes and the misuse of individual’s data. Provisions The Bill introduces specific offences for knowingly misusing an individual’s name, photograph, voice or likeness to cause harm. The Minister for Justice shall be required to carry out a review after one year of the Bill’s operation. Malcolm Byrne TD, Aibreán, 2025.

title: Housing Loans Regulations (Fresh Start - Buyout) (Amendment) Bill 2026
excerpt: ___________ An Bille fá na Rialacháin um Iasachtaí Tithíochta (Tosú as an Nua – Ceannach Thar Barr Amach) (Leasú), 2026 Housing Loans Regulations (Fresh Start – Buyout) (Amendment) Bill 2026 ___________ Meabhrán Míniúcháin Explanatory Memorandum ___________ 1 ____________ AN BILLE FÁ NA RIALACHÁIN UM IASACHTAÍ TITHÍOCHTA (TOSÚ AS AN NUA – CEANNACH THAR BARR AMACH) (LEASÚ), 2026 HOUSING LOANS REGULATIONS (FRESH START – BUYOUT) (AMENDMENT) BILL 2026 ____________ EXPLANATORY MEMORANDUM ____________ Purpose of the bill The purpose of the bill is to amend the Housing Loans Regulations 2021 (S.I. No. 701 of 2021) so as to allow persons who are remaining in the family home following a divorce or legal separation, and who need mortgage finance to buyout their former partner’s share of the family home, to apply to a local authority for a housing loan. Section 1 proposes to amend Regulation 7 of the Housing Loans Regulations 2021, by inserting a new paragraph (5) which would have the effect of extending the eligibility criteria of persons allowed to apply for a housing loan to persons who retain ownership of the family home after a divorce or legal separation and who need to apply for a housing loan for the purposes of buying out their former partners interest in the property. Section 2 is the standard short title and citation section. Eoin Ó Broin, TD, Márta, 2026.

title: Repeal of Exempted Development Regulations Bill 2026
excerpt: ___________ An Bille fá na Rialacháin um Fhorbairt Dhíolmhaithe a Aisghairm, 2026 Repeal of Exempted Development Regulations Bill 2026 ___________ Meabhrán Míniúcháin Explanatory Memorandum ___________ 1 ____________ AN BILLE FÁ NA RIALACHÁIN UM FHORBAIRT DHÍOLMHAITHE A AISGHAIRM, 2026 REPEAL OF EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT REGULATIONS BILL 2026 ____________ EXPLANATORY MEMORANDUM ____________ The purpose of this Bill is to repeal two exempted development regulations from 2022 and 2023 related to the provision of temporary accommodation for persons seeking international protection or in receipt of temporary protection Section 1: This section sets out the definitions relevant to the Bill Section 2: This section repeals S.I. 605/2022 granting exempted development status to certain categories of buildings to be used for the provision of accommodation for persons seeking international protection and S.I. 376/2023 which extended the provisions of S.I. 605/2022 to the provision of accommodation for persons in receipt of temporary protection and to extend the duration of the exemption from 2024 to 2028 Section 3: This is a transitional provision which allows the state agency responsible for providing accommodation for persons seeking internation protection or in receipt of temporary protection to seek planning retention permission for accommodation that had been granted exempted development status and needs to be regularised in order to continue to be used for this purpose. Section 4: This section sets out the short title of the Bill Eoin Ó Broin TD and Matt Carthy, Feabhra, 2026.

Scheme of leave for injuries 2. Short title [No. 85 of 2025] ACTS REFERRED TO Education Act 1998 (No. 51) Medical Practitioners Act 2007 (No. 25) Safety, Health and Welfare at Work Act 2005 (No. 10) Teaching Council Act 2001 (No. 8) 2 AN BILLE OIDEACHAIS (SAOIRE I LEITH DÍOBHÁLACHA), 2025 EDUCATION (LEAVE FOR INJURIES) BILL 2025 Bill entitled An Act to establish standards for any scheme maintained by the Minister for Education and Youth relating to the provision of leave of absence for teachers and special needs assistants who suffer certain injuries; and to provide for related matters. Be it enacted by the Oireachtas as follows: Scheme of leave for injuries 1. (1) This section applies to any scheme that is, or is to be, maintained by the Minister providing for leave of absence from work following injury suffered by a teacher or SNA who is employed in an approved position of employment in a recognised school. (2) A scheme to which this section applies shall satisfy the following conditions: (a) the scheme shall be in accordance with an agreement negotiated with recognised trade unions or staff associations representing the teachers or SNAs concerned; (b) the scheme shall include provision for immediate financial assistance to cover the medical and ancillary expenses of the teacher or SNA; (c) the scheme shall include provision, in cases where the nature or scale of injury suffered is not immediately apparent, for paid leave of absence to be commenced within a reasonable period of it being established that the injury concerned has been suffered; (d) subject to any provisions to which paragraph (e) applies, the scheme shall provide for paid leave of absence from work for the duration of any period in respect of which a certificate signed by a registered medical practitioner is provided, stating that the teacher or SNA is unable to return to work as a result of the injury concerned; (e) the scheme shall provide for early retirement in cases of long-term or permanent incapacity to return to work; (f) the scheme shall include provision for information about and access to support services including, where relevant, appropriate specialist services, including psychological support services; (g) the scheme shall outline the nature and extent of the duties of the school where a teacher or SNA suffers an injury to which the scheme applies, for the purposes of 3 5 10 15 20 25 30 ensuring compliance by the school with its duties under Part 3 of the Safety, Health and Welfare at Work Act 2005; (h) the scheme shall not discriminate between teachers and SNAs in relation to the availability or extent of entitlements under the scheme. (3) In this section— “approved position of employment” means a position of employment in a recognised school that is, for the purpose of being remunerated out of monies provided by the Oireachtas, approved by the Minister under section 24 of the Education Act 1998; “injury” means a physical or mental injury or illness and includes an injury suffered by a teacher or SNA in the course of his or her employment which is caused by an act of a student that— (a) directly or indirectly applies force to or causes an impact on his or her body, or (b) causes him or her to believe on reasonable grounds that he or she is likely immediately to be subjected to any such force or impact, and (c) if done by a person of full age and capacity, constitutes an assault or offence, regardless as to whether the act concerned was done intentionally, recklessly or otherwise; “Minister” means the Minister for Education and Youth; “recognised school” has the same meaning as in the Education Act 1998; “registered medical practitioner” has the same meaning as it has in the Medical Practitioners Act 2007; “SNA”— (a) means a special needs assistant within the meaning of the Special Needs Assistant Scheme published and maintained by the Minister, and (b) includes any other person, howsoever described, who is employed pursuant to a scheme maintained by the Minister to assist in relation to the special needs of students with disabilities in recognised schools; “teacher” means a registered teacher within the meaning of the Teaching Council Act 2001. excerpt: An Bille um Pá Íosta Náisiúnta (Daoine Óga, Printísigh agus Intéirnigh a Áireamh), 2025 National Minimum Wage (Inclusion of Young Persons, Apprentices and Interns) Bill 2025 Mar a tionscnaíodh As initiated [No. 80 of 2025] AN BILLE UM PÁ ÍOSTA NÁISIÚNTA (DAOINE ÓGA, PRINTÍSIGH AGUS INTÉIRNIGH A ÁIREAMH), 2025 NATIONAL MINIMUM WAGE (INCLUSION OF YOUNG PERSONS, APPRENTICES AND INTERNS) BILL 2025 Mar a tionscnaíodh As initiated CONTENTS Section 1. Definition 2. Amendment of Act of 2000: young persons 3. Amendment of Act of 2000: apprentices 4. Amendment of Act of 2000: interns 5. Short title, collective citation and construction [No. 80 of 2025] ACTS REFERRED TO Industrial Training Act 1967 (No. 5) Labour Services Act 1987 (No. 15) National Minimum Wage Act 2000 (No. 5) National Minimum Wage Acts 2000 and 2015 2 AN BILLE UM PÁ ÍOSTA NÁISIÚNTA (DAOINE ÓGA, PRINTÍSIGH AGUS INTÉIRNIGH A ÁIREAMH), 2025 NATIONAL MINIMUM WAGE (INCLUSION OF YOUNG PERSONS, APPRENTICES AND INTERNS) BILL 2025 Bill entitled An Act to provide for the entitlement of employed young persons to the full national minimum hourly rate of pay; to provide for the inclusion of apprentices within the application of the National Minimum Wage Acts 2000 and 2015; to provide for the payment of the national minimum wage to certain persons doing work as interns or on work experience; for these purposes to amend the National Minimum Wage Act 2000 ; and to provide for related matters. Be it enacted by the Oireachtas as follows: Definition 1. In this Act, “Act of 2000” means the National Minimum Wage Act 2000. Amendment of Act of 2000: young persons 2. The Act of 2000 is amended— (a) by the deletion of section 14 and the substitution of the following: “14. Subject to sections 17, 18 and 41, an employee shall be remunerated by his or her employer in respect of the employee’s working hours in any pay reference period, at an hourly rate of pay that on average is not less than the national minimum hourly rate of pay.”, and (b) by the deletion of section 15. Amendment of Act of 2000: apprentices 3. The Act of 2000 is amended— (a) in section 2(1), in the definition of “contract of employment”, by the deletion of paragraph (a) and the substitution of the following: “(a) a contract of service or apprenticeship (including an apprenticeship within the meaning of or under the Industrial Training Act 1967 or 3 5 10 15 20 25 the Labour Services Act 1987), or”, and (b) in section 5, by the deletion of subsection (1)(b). Amendment of Act of 2000: interns 4. The Act of 2000 is amended in section 2 by the insertion of the following subsection after subsection (2)— “(2A) (a) Subject to paragraph (b), a person (‘the worker’) who does more than 30 hours of work within any period of four weeks for another person is an employee for the purposes of this Act, notwithstanding that— (i) he or she has not entered into and does not work under a contract of employment, and (ii) he or she is referred to or described as a trainee or an intern or as a person on work experience. (b) Paragraph (a) does not apply if the worker does not expect and has no reason to expect payment for his or her work, and— (i) the work is done for charitable or philanthropic reasons, or (ii) (I) the worker is undergoing a programme of education and training leading to an award recognised by the Qualifications and Quality Assurance Authority of Ireland, and (II) work of the nature done by the worker is prescribed by the education and training provider concerned for persons undertaking that programme.”. Short title, collective citation and construction 5. (1) This Act may be cited as the National Minimum Wage (Inclusion of Young Persons, Apprentices and Interns) Act 2025. (2) This Act and the National Minimum Wage Acts 2000 and 2015 may be cited together as the National Minimum Wage Acts 2000 to 2025 and shall be construed together as one Act. 4 5 10 15 20 25 30 5 An Bille um Pá Íosta Náisiúnta (Daoine Óga, Printísigh agus Intéirnigh a Áireamh), 2025 BILLE (mar a tionscnaíodh) dá ngairtear Acht do dhéanamh socrú maidir le daoine óga fostaithe a bheith i dteideal an lánráta pá íosta náisiúnta san uair an chloig; do dhéanamh socrú maidir le printísigh a áireamh laistigh d’fheidhm na nAchtanna um Pá Íosta Náisiúnta, 2000 agus 2015; do dhéanamh socrú maidir leis an bpá íosta náisiúnta a íoc le daoine áirithe a bheidh ag obair mar intéirnigh nó ag gabháil do thaithí oibre; chun na gcríoch sin, do leasú an Achta um Pá Íosta Náisi

excerpt: An Bille um Fhoréigean Baile (Scéim Saorthaistil), 2025 Domestic Violence (Free Travel Scheme) Bill 2025 Mar a tionscnaíodh As initiated [No. 59 of 2025] AN BILLE UM FHORÉIGEAN BAILE (SCÉIM SAORTHAISTIL), 2025 DOMESTIC VIOLENCE (FREE TRAVEL SCHEME) BILL 2025 Mar a tionscnaíodh As initiated CONTENTS Section 1. Short title and commencement [No. 59 of 2025] ACT REFERRED TO Local Government Act 2001 (No. 37) 2 AN BILLE UM FHORÉIGEAN BAILE (SCÉIM SAORTHAISTIL), 2025 DOMESTIC VIOLENCE (FREE TRAVEL SCHEME) BILL 2025 Bill entitled An Act to establish a free travel scheme for victims fleeing domestic violence; and to provide for related matters. Be it enacted by the Oireachtas as follows: Duty to establish and operate free travel scheme for victims fleeing domestic violence 1. (1) The Minister for Social Protection shall establish and operate a scheme which provides free travel to victims of domestic violence who— (a) are fleeing, or have recently fled, domestic violence, and (b) are in need of a travel pass— (i) in order to flee domestic violence, or (ii) in the period immediately after fleeing domestic violence. (2) The scheme shall provide— (a) for a card or pass issued under the scheme to be valid for 3 months beginning with the day on which it is issued (subject to extension in exceptional circumstances by up to a further 3 months), (b) for free travel on the same transport services and at the same times as under the Free Travel Scheme, (c) for assessments of whether a person qualifies for free travel under the scheme (and assessments of whether exceptional circumstances justify extending the validity of a pass or card issued under the scheme) to be carried out by bodies or organisations approved for this purpose by the Minister for Social Protection after having consulted Cuan, (d) for such assessments, so far as is possible, to rely upon or be conducted at the same time as any other assessment conducted by one of the approved bodies or organisations for the purpose of determining whether a person is a victim of domestic violence and the person’s needs, (e) for the Department of Social Protection to issue a card or pass under the scheme as soon as is reasonably practicable after receiving an assessment from an approved body or organisation assessing a person as qualifying for free travel 3 5 10 15 20 25 30 under the scheme, unless the Department has reason to suspect fraud or misuse, (f) for a card or pass issued under the scheme to be available in the same forms available under the Free Travel Scheme, (g) for a card or pass issued under the scheme to be indistinguishable from a card or pass issued under the Free Travel Scheme (and for it not to otherwise identify the reason it was issued), (h) for information about the scheme to be in plain language and published in Irish, English and the 10 other most commonly spoken languages in Ireland. (3) In this section— “Cuan” means An Ghníomhaireacht um Fhoréigean Baile, Gnéasach agus Inscnebhunaithe; “Free Travel Scheme” means the Free Travel Scheme operated by the Department of Social Protection; “victim of domestic violence” includes a dependant of a victim of domestic violence (including any adult cared for by a victim of domestic violence). Annual report on operation of scheme 2. (1) The Minister for Social Protection shall publish a report, and lay it before each House of the Oireachtas, after the end of each year that the scheme established under section 1 is operational. (2) A report under subsection (1) shall include— (a) the number of cards or passes issued under the scheme in the scheme year to which the report relates (including the number issued to persons residing in each administrative area), (b) a summary of feedback on the scheme received by the Department of Social Protection from approved bodies and organisations, operators of transport services and victims of domestic violence during the scheme year to which the report relates, and (c) the Minister for Social Protection’s assessment of the effectiveness of the scheme and the action (if any) that the Minister intends to take to make the scheme more effective. (3) In this section— “administrative area” has the meaning given to it by section 2 of the Local Government Act 2001; “approved bodies and organisations” means bodies and organisations approved as referred to in section 1(2)(c

title: Protection of Retail Workers Bill 2025
excerpt: An Bille um Oibrithe Miondíola a Chosaint, 2025 Protection of Retail Workers Bill 2025 Mar a tionscnaíodh As initiated [No. 17 of 2025] AN BILLE UM OIBRITHE MIONDÍOLA A CHOSAINT, 2025 PROTECTION OF RETAIL WORKERS BILL 2025 Mar a tionscnaíodh As initiated CONTENTS Section 1. Interpretation 2. Offence of assaulting retail worker 3. Short title [No. 17 of 2025] ACTS REFERRED TO Criminal Justice (Public Order) Act 1994 (No. 2) Fines Act 2010 (No. 8) 2 AN BILLE UM OIBRITHE MIONDÍOLA A CHOSAINT, 2025 PROTECTION OF RETAIL WORKERS BILL 2025 Bill entitled An Act to amend the Criminal Justice (Public Order) Act 1994 to create specific offences for assaulting or threatening retail workers carrying out their employment. Be it enacted by the Oireachtas as follows: Interpretation 1. In this Act— “Act of 1994” means the Criminal Justice (Public Order) Act 1994; “Minister” means the Minister for Justice; “retail worker” means a person whose usual place of work is retail premises, or whose usual place of work is not retail premises but who does retail work, and includes— (a) in relation to a business that owns or occupies any premises in which the person works, a person who— (i) is an employee of the business, (ii) is an owner of the business, or (iii) works in the premises under arrangements made between the business and another person for the provision of staff, (b) a person who delivers goods from retail premises, whether or not the person receives payment for the work is irrelevant. Offence of assaulting retail worker 2. The Act of 1994 is amended, by the insertion of the following section after section 18: “18A. (1) It shall be an offence for a person to assault, threaten or abuse another person— (a) who is a retail worker, and (b) who is engaged, at the time, in retail work. (2) No offence is committed under subsection (1) unless the person who assaults, threatens or abuses knows or ought to know that the other person— 3 5 10 15 20 25 30 (a) is a retail worker, and (b) is engaged, at the time, in retail work. (3) A person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable, on summary conviction, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months and/or a fine not less than a class D fine as set out by the Fines Act 2010. (4) The offence under subsection (1) of threatening or abusing a retail worker is committed by a person only if the person— (a) behaves in a threatening or abusive manner towards the worker, and (b) intends by the behaviour to cause the worker or any other person fear or alarm or is reckless as to whether the behaviour would cause such fear or alarm. (5) Subsection (1) applies to— (a) behaviour of any kind including, in particular, things said or otherwise communicated as well as things done, (b) behaviour consisting of— (i) a single act, or (ii) a course of conduct.”. Short title 3. This Act may be cited as the Protection of Retail Workers Act 2025. 4 5 10 15 20 An Bille um Oibrithe Miondíola a Chosaint, 2025 BILLE (mar a tionscnaíodh) dá ngairtear Acht do leasú an Achta um Cheartas Coiriúil (Ord Poiblí), 1994 chun cionta sonracha a chruthú arb éard iad ionsaí nó bagairt a dhéanamh ar oibrithe miondíola atá ag gabháil dá bhfostaíocht. Na Seanadóirí Máire Nic Giolla Phádraig, Seosamh Ó Flaitheartaigh, Áine Ní Choinín agus Teresa Costello a thug isteach, 29 Aibreán, 2025 Protection of Retail Workers Bill 2025 BILL (as initiated) entitled An Act to amend the Criminal Justice (Public Order) Act 1994 to create specific offences for assaulting or threatening retail workers carrying out their employment. Short title and citation [No. 44 of 2024] ACT REFERRED TO Health Act 2007 (No. 23) 2 AN BILLE SLÁINTE (SEIRBHÍSÍ CÓIREÁLA SCOLÓISE), 2024 HEALTH (SCOLIOSIS TREATMENT SERVICES) BILL 2024 Bill entitled An Act to impose on the Health Service Executive certain special duties and powers in relation to the establishment of a specialised treatment service for the inpatient and outpatient treatment of children and adults of spinal scoliosis who are resident in the State and to confer certain duties and powers on the Minister for Health in relation to the service to be established and to provide for related matters. Be it enacted by the Oireachtas as follows: Scoliosis Treatment Service - Establishment 1. The Health Service Executive shall establish and maintain a national treatment service for the timely and effective inpatient and outpatient treatment of scoliosis within the State at such hospitals and other clinics and centres as it may designate for the timely detection, assessment and remedial treatment of scoliosis for all children and adults normally resident in the State. Provision of resources 2. It shall be the duty of the Health Service Executive to provide and make available adequate resources for the carrying on of the service, including the retention, engagement and remuneration of specialist surgeons, clinicians, medical practitioners, nurses, physiotherapists and other therapists, and treatment facilities including surgical facilities, as are necessary to enable it to comply with its obligations under section 1 to the highest standards and in the most timely fashion. Services within State 3. The Health Service Executive may comply with its duty under section 1 at such hospitals, clinics and centres as are under its direct control or management or at other suitable hospitals, centres or clinics within the State as it may direct. Services outside State 4. The Health Service Executive may also, where necessary, comply with its duty under section 1 to individual patients by arranging for the provision of such services by agreement at hospitals, clinics, and centres outside the State where for practical reasons 3 5 10 15 20 25 30 the timely and urgent provision of such services at the standard referred to in section 2 so requires. Report and survey 5. The Health Service Executive shall every four months or more frequently, commencing three months after the passing of this Act, furnish to the Minister for Health a report and survey under section 6. Information 6. The report and survey provided for in section 5 shall include an up to date analysis of the need and demand for scoliosis services to be provided under section 1, the time periods within which such services, including treatments are intended to be carried out, whether the resources to be deployed in the provision of the services are sufficient, and any delays anticipated in their provision, whether guidelines issued by the Minister for Health under section 8 are being complied with, and up to date information as to waiting lists. Laying of reports 7. The Minister for Health shall lay all reports received by him or her under section 6 before the Houses of the Oireachtas for their information and consideration not later than 14 days after their receipt. Guidelines 8. The Minister for Health shall, not later than 4 months after the passing of this Act and from time to time thereafter, having consulted with the Health Service Executive, issue and publish guidelines for the time periods within which services provided under section 1 and 2 are required to be provided in a timely or most timely fashion, and it shall be the duty of the Health Service Executive to comply with such guidelines. Laying of guidelines 9. The Minister for Health shall lay all guidelines issued by him or her under section 8 before the Houses of the Oireachtas not later than 7 days after their issuance. Be it enacted by the Oireachtas as follows: Amendment of Maternity Protection Act 1994 1. (1) The Maternity Protection Act 1994 is amended— (a) by inserting the following section after section 14B: “Postponement of maternity leave or additional maternity leave in event of cancer diagnosis or treatment 14C. (1)Notwithstanding the entitlement to terminate leave as provided for in section 14A and subject to subsection (2), an employee who is on maternity leave or is entitled to, or is on, additional maternity leave may, if such person is diagnosed with cancer or is being treated for cancer, request in writing (or cause a written request to be submitted to) her employer to postpone— (a) part of the maternity leave, (b) part of the maternity leave and the additional maternity leave, or (c) the additional maternity leave or part of it, as may be appropriate, in accordance with this section. (2) An employee may make a request under paragraph (a) or (b) of subsection (1) to postpone part of her maternity leave with effect from a date she selects only if the period of maternity leave taken by her on that date is not less than 14 weeks and not less than 4 of those weeks are after the end of the week of confinement. (3) Notwithstanding the fact that an employee who is on maternity leave has not in accordance with section 14(4) notified her employer in writing (or caused her employer to be so notified) of her intention to take additional maternity leave, she shall be deemed, for the purposes 3 5 10 15 20 25 30 of making a request under paragraph (b) or (c) of subsection (1), to have complied with section 14(4). (4) An employer who receives a request under subsection (1) may agree to postpone the leave concerned and, if the employer does so— (a) the employee concerned shall return to work on a date agreed by her and the employer that is not later than the date on which the leave concerned is due to end in accordance with the notification given, or deemed under subsection (3) to have been given, by the employee to the employer under section 9 or 14, as the case may be, (b) the leave concerned shall be postponed with effect from the date agreed under paragraph (a), and (c) the employee concerned shall be entitled to— (i) the part of the maternity leave, (ii) the part of the maternity leave and the additional maternity leave, or (iii) the additional maternity leave or the part of it, as the case may be, not taken by her by reason of the postponement (in this section referred to as ‘resumed leave’) in accordance with regulations made under this section by the Minister to be taken in one continuous period commencing not later than 7 days after being certified by a registered medical practitioner fit to return to work. (5) An employer who receives a request under subsection (1) shall notify the employee concerned in writing of the employer’s decision in relation to the request as soon as reasonably practicable following the receipt of it. (6) Without prejudice to the generality of subsection (4), regulations under this section may make provision in relation to either or both of the following matters: (a) the maximum period of postponement of leave under this section, and (b) the evidence to be furnished by an employee to her employer. Short title and commencement [No. 71 of 2024] ACT REFERRED TO Domestic Violence Act 2018 (No. 6) 2 AN BILLE UM FHORÉIGEAN BAILE (LEASÚ) (UIMH. 3), 2024 DOMESTIC VIOLENCE (AMENDMENT) (NO. 3) BILL 2024 Bill entitled An Act to amend the Domestic Violence Act 2018 in relation to the offence of coercive control by extending the meaning assigned in section 39 of that Act to the term relevant person and to provide for related matters. Be it enacted by the Oireachtas as follows: Amendment of Domestic Violence Act 2018 1. Section 39 of the Domestic Violence Act 2018 is amended by substituting the following subsections for subsection (4): “(4) In this section, a person is a ‘relevant person’ in respect of another person if the first-named person— (a) is, or has been, the spouse or civil partner of the said other person, (b) is, or has been, party to an agreement to marry the said other person, (c) is, or has been, in an intimate relationship with the said other person, (d) is a parent, adoptive parent, grandparent, great-grandparent, child, brother, sister, first cousin, uncle, aunt, nephew or niece, whether of the whole blood, half blood or by marriage or civil partnership of the said other person or that other person’s spouse, former spouse, civil partner or former civil partner, or (e) is eligible to make an application under section 6C(2)(a) of the Act of 1964 in respect of a child of the said other person. (5) The definition of ‘child’ in section 2(1) does not apply for the purposes of this section. (6) Except in the case of behaviour described under subsection (2)(a), it shall be a defence for a person charged with an offence under subsection (1) to prove that at the time of the alleged offence— (a) that person believed that he or she was acting in the best interests of the relevant person, and 3 5 10 15 20 25 30 (b) such behaviour was, in the circumstances, reasonable.”. Short title and commencement 2. (1) This Act may be cited as the Domestic Violence (Amendment)(No. 3) Act 2024. (2) This Act comes into operation 3 months after the date of its passing or on such earlier date than the said 3 months as the Minister for Justice may by order appoint. 4 5 An Bille um Fhoréigean Baile (Leasú) (Uimh. 3), 2024 BILLE (mar a tionscnaíodh) dá ngairtear Acht do leasú an Achta um Fhoréigean Baile, 2018 i ndáil leis an gcion arb éard é smachtú comhéigneach tríd an mbrí a shanntar don téarma “duine iomchuí” in alt 39 den Acht sin a leathnú agus do dhéanamh socrú i dtaobh nithe gaolmhara.
